messages:
taylor: Heads-up — ran into a "window-starvation" scenario in go-sdk@0.9.1 while running our bulk-embed sample. Inflight window stopped making progress under sustained 401s + retry jitter.

nish: Oof. Which sample and config?

taylor: sampleapps/bulk-embed-go, AggregatePaginator with Concurrency=12, WindowSize=512. Repro is easy: mock auth to return 401s for one second every 10s. After a couple cycles, the paginator stops issuing outbound requests but the process doesn't crash — looks like something holds the window token.

sam: Any logs or a minimal stack?

taylor: Pulled logs from the run, trimming noise:
```
2026-12-08T09:02:15.102Z DEBUG paginator: acquire-window-token
2026-12-08T09:02:15.103Z DEBUG transport: request -> /v1/embeds (id=345)
2026-12-08T09:02:15.104Z DEBUG transport: response 401 id=345
2026-12-08T09:02:15.105Z DEBUG auth: start-refresh (singleflight: miss)
2026-12-08T09:02:15.106Z DEBUG paginator: holding-window (id=345)
2026-12-08T09:02:16.250Z DEBUG auth: refresh-complete, token=tok_abc
2026-12-08T09:02:16.251Z DEBUG paginator: waiting on-window-token (blocked)
// then silence: no more outgoing requests
```

taylor: The refresh completes but the window token never gets released; other goroutines are blocked waiting for the token.

nish: Sounds like auth refresh path tries to requeue or mutate the same window state and ends up blocked behind a mutex it also expects to be free. Could be a reentrant lock bug in the Go paginator.

sam: Is this Go-only? Python and Node sampleapps didn't exhibit the freeze in my quick runs. They either queue refreshes or avoid holding the inflight token across network ops.

taylor: Correct. Go SDK kept an internal mutex across the full request lifecycle, including auth refresh callbacks. When refresh triggered, the callback tried to drain pending events under the same mutex -> live lock.

nish: Two-pronged fix: (A) don't hold the inflight-window mutex while performing network ops (including refresh), or (B) make refresh singleflight and external to window code path. I prefer B for safety: keep window invariants tightly controlled, and make auth a separate singleflight that doesn't touch window bookkeeping.

sam: +1. Also add an opt-in Paginator config: ReleaseOnAuth bool (default false) so users can try safe fallback without an SDK upgrade. And optionally WindowHoldWarnMs to emit diagnostics when a token is held too long.

taylor: I prototyped a small patch: auth.SingleFlight() in auth package; Paginator calls auth.RequestToken(ctx) outside of the window lock if RequestToken may block. It freed the hang in my runs. I'll push a tiny repro branch.

ci-bot: CI started for branch taylor/go-paginator-auth-repro #5

nish: For parity, update go-sdk docs and add the single-flight helper to go/auth and a note in SDK parity matrix. Also add e2e in devex/e2e that simulates auth pulses under concurrency.

sam: Tests: unit test for singleflight ensures only 1 refresh runs under N callers; e2e verifies no stalls with 50 concurrent inflight tokens. Also add a chaos test that randomly returns 401/500 for short bursts.

ops-bot: Observability note: log window token holder's goroutine stack on WindowHoldWarnMs threshold breach and emit a metric paginator.window_hold_seconds.

taylor: Pushed branch + small repro harness. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/sampleapps/pull/331 (includes e2e, singleflight util, and optional WindowHoldWarnMs).

ci-bot: CI passed for PR taylor/go-paginator-auth-repro #331 (unit: 9/9, e2e: 1/1) :white_check_mark:

nish: Follow-up: add docs on customer-facing mitigation (pin older go-sdk or set ReleaseOnAuth=true). Also coordinate a patch release with eng-releases so enterprise customers can get the fix fast.

sam: I'll take the release notes and coordinate the backport to 0.9.2 and 0.9.3. Also add a short FAQ in devex about "hangs during auth storms" explaining the race and recommended settings.

taylor: Thanks all. Saved us from an on-call page.
